summary: Implement metadata-only connector bootstrap previews, tenant-scoped resumable initial-import dispatch jobs and durable interval schedules through the existing provider-neutral sync/reconciliation boundaries.

impacts.evidence: Preview, schedule and job rows carry organization/workspace identity under forced RLS; the cross-tenant claim returns scope and all subsequent operations reapply it.
Only policy counts, versions, bounded checkpoints and machine error codes are stored; credentials, provider payloads and personal data are excluded.
OpenAPI 0.12.0 adds four additive operations and generated SDKs are regenerated; route parity covers 75 paths and 88 operations.
No event schema changes; control-plane changes use existing append-only application audit records.
The frozen connector runtime is unchanged; provider-neutral sync capability mapping is exported from the existing host-owned Connector SDK package for API and scheduler reuse.
Expand migrations 000062-000063 add forced-RLS metadata, schedules, lease jobs and a forward-only PL/pgSQL name-resolution fix.
Preview and scheduler execution fail closed on account health and current per-account capabilities; the privileged claim function is narrow, bounded and revoked from PUBLIC.
Schedule configuration is audited as write-sensitive, and existing per-capability approval metadata remains mandatory for remote writes.
Preview, initial-import queueing and schedule updates produce bounded tenant-scoped audit entries; reconciliation runs retain operational evidence.
Stable policy ordering, checkpoint_policy_id and deterministic job/policy run IDs make lease replay resumable without duplicate reconciliation runs.
Dry-run performs no egress and the scheduler creates existing reconciliation work only; no destination policy changes.
GET bootstrap state exposes bounded schedules, attempts, fan-out checkpoints and safe error codes; reconciliation status exposes actual import/drift progress.
Operators can disable schedules and stop the scheduler without deleting evidence; deploy migrations before the new scheduler and retain tables through rollback.
Domain, API, scheduler determinism, migration, OpenAPI parity, SDK, frontend and live PostgreSQL claim tests cover the Task-108 boundary.
